open_points.subject: A9 deployment route
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
open_points.question: Is this the Factory deployment gate, another deployment pipeline, the service's HTTPS host route, or a route shared with the Client Portal?
options: The Factory deployment gate dedicated to this service
A non-Factory deployment pipeline dedicated to this service
The same deployment pipeline used by the Client Portal
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a service-specific Factory deployment gate analogous to the Client Portal's gate.

witness.initial: A release image is ready and both the Client Portal deployment pipeline and a separate service deployment mechanism exist.
events: A deployer asks the implementation to perform the rule 2 vulnerability check.
One implementer attaches the check to the Client Portal's existing deployment pipeline.
Another implementer builds a separate route for this service.
outcomes: The image can be deployed only through the Portal's existing pipeline.
The image is deployed through a distinct service pipeline with independently configured policy.
witness.observer: The deployer and the security reviewer

open_points.subject: A9 rule 2 and INV-15
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
open_points.question: Must every possible deployment be admitted through this route, or is using the route only the prescribed procedure while another deployment path may exist?
options: The route is the exclusive technical admission path
Other paths may exist but must independently run the same check
The rule is procedural and does not technically block bypass deployment
open_points.default_guess: Make the route the exclusive technical admission path.

witness.initial: A service image contains an installed distribution with a vulnerability listed in the accepted OSV snapshot.
events: An operator attempts the normal deployment route, which refuses the image.
The operator then invokes a lower-level deployment mechanism directly.
outcomes: The lower-level mechanism is inaccessible or refuses the image, so INV-15 holds.
The direct deployment succeeds because the text no longer says deployment is admitted only through the checked route.
witness.observer: The operator and users exposed to the deployed service

open_points.subject: INV-15 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-15: the deployment route refuses an image holding a distribution with a known vulnerability, and refuses when the check cannot complete.
open_points.question: What must the Required tests item show to establish the invariant that no vulnerable distribution is deployed, including the absence or enforcement of deployment paths that bypass the tested route?
options: Show that the tested route is the only deployment admission path
Test every deployment path and show each enforces rule 2
Narrow INV-15 to deployments attempted through this route
open_points.default_guess: Add a check proving that the tested route is the only deployment admission path.

witness.initial: The checked route refuses a vulnerable image, while a direct platform deployment entry point also exists.
events: The witness check exercises only the named deployment route.
A deployer submits the same image through the direct entry point.
outcomes: The Required test passes although the vulnerable image is deployed.
The invariant is considered proven only after the direct entry point is shown unavailable or equally guarded.

open_points.subject: A9 rule 2 current snapshot
open_points.text: Before each deployment every distribution installed in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts as current. That route owns the age limit, and no code of this service reads it.
open_points.question: Which clock supplies the instant used to decide whether the snapshot is current, in what representation are the snapshot time and current time compared, how many clock readings does one deployment check take, and what exact boundary applies at the age limit?
options: One UTC clock reading per deployment check, compared to a UTC snapshot timestamp; equality passes
One UTC clock reading per deployment check; equality fails
The deployment platform supplies a precomputed current/not-current decision
The route may read its clock more than once
open_points.default_guess: Use one aware UTC clock reading for the whole check, compare it with an aware UTC snapshot timestamp, and allow an age equal to the limit.

witness.initial: The OSV snapshot's age is exactly the configured age limit while the clock advances across that boundary during the deployment check.
events: The deployment route begins checking the image.
The route determines whether the snapshot is current.
The route either admits or refuses the image.
outcomes: A single initial reading and an inclusive boundary make the snapshot current, so the image may proceed.
A later reading or an exclusive boundary makes the snapshot stale, so deployment is refused.

open_points.subject: A9 Consequence
open_points.text: The check of rule 2 is built: it is the deployment route of this service, as it is the Client Portal's.
open_points.rule: Доказательство — декларация, а не проза: фраза «её читает гейт» читателя не доказывает.
